title: Course Syllabus
markdown:
## What this covers

This chapter is not a lecture but the course syllabus: it states what Statistics 205A covers over
the semester and what background it assumes, so that the rest of the chapters can be read against
a sense of where they sit in the sequence. It assumes nothing beyond ordinary familiarity with a
course syllabus.

## Scope of the course

Statistics 205A is designed as a sequence together with Statistics C205B/Mathematics C218B, under
a combined syllabus. Over the two courses, the material runs:

- measure theory, to the extent needed for probability
- expectation and distributions
- laws of large numbers and central limit theorems for independent random variables
- characteristic function methods
- conditional expectation, martingales, and martingale convergence theorems
- Markov chains
- stationary processes
- Brownian motion

## Format

The course runs 15 weeks, with 3 hours of lecture per week.

## Prerequisites

The course assumes some knowledge of real analysis and metric spaces, including compactness and
the Riemann integral. Knowledge of the Lebesgue integral and/or elementary probability is helpful
but not essential, given an otherwise strong mathematical background.

## Sources

This chapter is drawn entirely from the course syllabus page supplied as notes:
`probability/berkeley/stat205a/fall-2024/syllabus.md` (converted from `syllabus.qmd`, CC BY 4.0).
No slides, transcript, or exercises were supplied for this entry, and the syllabus itself contains
no lecture content beyond the scope, format, and prerequisites reproduced above — so this chapter
is correspondingly short rather than padded with material the source does not contain.
